design.title: Metric edge and signed-wall-distance diffusion
design.coverage_gap: This D10 has five LL and five HH episodes but no LH/HL. Goal minus object x is consequently small in support, even though initial hand-to-object x varies in sign. Per-coordinate support standardization can make a new cross-sign relation extreme. A raw global encoder can also confuse goal x with object x. This candidate exposes their differences explicitly at a fixed physical scale, without estimating the narrow goal-object x variance.
design.reusable_regularity: Manipulation is organized by hand-object and object-goal differences, while a finite obstacle requires signed distances to its faces rather than an assumption of free-space translation symmetry. A fixed 64-feature representation supplies both displacement vectors and axis-aligned box features. All metric relations share a 0.1 m scale; current-minus-native-previous displacements use the public 0.01 m action scale. These are unit choices, not fitted controller gains. Only the common conditional U-Net is learned; there is no stage switch, controller, planner, or extra loss.
dependencies_preserved: Robot/world position: absolute hand and wall centers at 0.5 m scale preserve the world origin and fixed robot workspace. Other current and previous positions can be recovered from these and the supplied edges/increments.

Object interaction: hand-object vector, previous hand-object vector, horizontal and 3D separation, aperture and aperture difference, both object xyzw quaternions, and both hand/object causal increments.
Goal: goal-object, goal-hand and goal-wall vectors retain all three coordinates, including varying goal height.
Obstacle: observed wall center and all three half-sizes, six signed inside-face distances for both hand and object, and both box signed-distance scalars. No collision-free path is computed.
Fixed world axes and native gripper anisotropy are not quotiented away. Only object2 channels declared absent zeros are omitted.

evidence_refs.use: Establishes exactly ten current support episodes and no development/test evidence.
LL/HH training versus cross-sign C and larger-magnitude E; runtime fields, world action semantics, fixed orientation.

Five episodes per training cell; examples demo_00 and demo_01 show very small initial goal-object x difference and different goal heights. Wall center (0.1,0.75,0.06) and half-size (0.12,0.01,0.06) require preserving finite wall geometry.
Actual initial hand/object/goal and finite wall layout inspected.
Actual raised grasp before crossing inspected.
Actual transported object near elevated goal inspected.

Causal aperture and hand-object vertical offset distinguish descent/grasp and ascent. Vertical lift is followed by horizontal transport while retaining grip. This motivates preserving temporal increments and wall clearance rather than just endpoint differences.
64 features per each of two observations; unchanged common DP, action loss, execution and deployment interface.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit metric edges do not prevent shortcut learning, LH/HL failures should exhibit lateral transport remaining near initial object x instead of following goal x, despite successful grasp/lift.
Without an explicit stage latent, slow closure or missed grasps may be followed by premature lift/transport. Aperture and vertical increments are available but not hard-coded as a controller.

Signed point-box distances do not model finger/object swept volumes. Near-wall or edge contacts can persist even when point clearance is positive. Larger displacements remain an unmeasured extrapolation challenge.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45] only; each whole observation includes its native previous state
required_runtime_fields.not_used: Absent object2 channels, IDs, time, future labels, success flags, environment handles and normalized raw history. All necessary present physical state is retained through the representation.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: first three outputs remain native world_dx/world_dy/world_dz with 0.01 m scale, fourth remains native gripper controlling [g,-g]. No candidate clipping. Host alone clips decoded native actions and executes four of sixteen.

design.support_fit: None. No fitted state or cached support labels at deployment.
design.change_summary: Initial scientific design, not a clone or performance-driven revision. Fixed metric relational representation plus finite-wall signed geometry; single unchanged four-channel common diffusion model. No structural repairs as authored.
